Target-process identity has not been verified. A saved profile or matching configuration file does not prove what another app sees.
Apps inherit this saved default unless they have a custom policy. Saving does not activate an engine.
Observed values come from this MaxManager process and may already be changed by an external global module. They are not certified real hardware values.
Shared with Device Identity. Changes appear in both screens; this policy is independent of performance settings.

An external global hook cannot be undone by removing an app assignment. This combination needs a process-isolation adapter and is blocked from apply.
Choose a profile to enable Custom. Editing a shared profile updates every app that references it.
Choose an app or enter a valid package name.
Identity fields must be non-empty. An optional fingerprint must use the Android format and match brand/product/device. No identifiers or framework API-level changes.
Invalid identity or conflicting fingerprint. Fix the values before saving.
This imported profile contains a legacy API-level value. Preparation refuses it; saving this editor clears it without changing the host framework.
Delete %1$s? Its app assignments become Disabled instead of silently inheriting Global. A saved global reference is cleared. Engine configuration is unchanged until explicitly applied.

This prepares the latest saved configuration through the control arbiter. Global and per-app files are separate operations, not one atomic transaction. Root may be requested. Configuration read-back is checked; process identity is not. External module lifecycle/reboot may be needed. A private recovery record is saved before writing; configuration recovery remains available after restarting MaxManager. Confirm only on a device you own or are authorized to test.
These states describe adapter/configuration eligibility, not universal Android hook support. No writable control exists for an unimplemented surface.

Prepares COPG-VD JSON only; does not execute resetprop or reboot. Existing advanced fields are refused rather than erased. Global runtime apply, cross-engine ordering, property-level reboot recovery, and app isolation still require an adapter/device verification.

Restore the previous configuration saved before the latest transaction, even after restarting MaxManager. This restores a file, not live properties or running app processes. An unreadable file or external modification blocks restore. No automatic root request or restore on startup.
Recovery storage could not be verified. Writes are blocked; do not delete the journal before reviewing it.

Independent global and per-app injection layers are both present. Their ordering/isolation is unverified; preparation is blocked rather than promising a custom app identity.
